events.name: Family Fun Day — Charity Booth
events.desc: Our first on-campus event of the year: a games booth raising funds for local ASD programs.
detail: Family Fun Day is one of AISG's biggest community celebrations, and Itod GCED runs its own charity booth right in the middle of it. We design and host carnival-style games — ring toss, lucky draws and more — that families play for a small donation.
Every dollar raised goes to local autism support programs and partner organisations in Guangzhou, so the games we run directly fund real services for the ASD community.
As a member you might run a game, manage the cash box, decorate the booth, or explain our cause to visitors. No experience needed — we train you on the day.

events.name: ImpactGZ Service Learning Summit
events.desc: We visit our partner school to run translation booths and lead inclusive workshops.
detail: The ImpactGZ Service Learning Summit is the annual gathering of AISG's GCED service leaders and our partner organisations. Our club runs two things there: translation booths that help visitors connect with partner groups, and inclusive workshops designed to be played together.

Our signature workshop, 'Joining Hands, Cracking the Code Together', features games like Water Fetch, Tower of Hanoi and Da Vinci Code — activities that are fun precisely because they need cooperation, not speed.
It's a chance to represent Itod GCED to the wider Guangzhou service community and to see what other schools and NGOs are doing for inclusion.

events.name: Lingnan Campus Visit
events.desc: Full-team visit to Lingnan — cooking, sports and games with autistic students.
detail: We have a close partnership with Lingnan Modern Technician College (岭南现代技师学院), whose community includes many autistic students. Each visit we travel as a full team and spend the afternoon cooking, playing sports and doing games side by side with them.

The relationship works both ways: in 2026, 20 Lingnan students visited our Science City campus for a tour, an art collaboration and performances — and we regularly go to them for the same kind of shared day.
Members pair up as buddies for the afternoon — the simplest and most meaningful job in the club.

events.name: Holiday Bazaar
events.desc: Year-end fundraising market with games and student-made goods.
detail: The Holiday Bazaar is our year-end fundraising market and a December tradition going back to the club's earliest years. We set up games stalls and sell student-made goods — from baked treats to crafts — with all proceeds going to local ASD support programs.
It's the club's biggest fundraising push of the year and a chance for the whole school community to get involved before the winter break.
Members help design the stalls, bake or craft the goods, run the games, and handle sales on the night.

events.name: International Day
events.desc: Campus-wide awareness day celebrating neurodiversity and inclusion.
detail: International Day is a campus-wide celebration of the many cultures and identities at AISG — and for us, it's also a day to celebrate neurodiversity. Our booth shares what autism is (and isn't), with simple facts, stories and activities that invite curiosity instead of pity.
We join the celebration on both campuses across the year, making sure the message of inclusion is part of the biggest days on the school calendar.
Members take shifts at the booth explaining our work, running mini-games and handing out our awareness materials.
